memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So he went and got them and brought them to his mother, and she prepared some tasty food, just the way his father liked it. Then Rebekah took the best clothes of Esau her older son, which she had in the house, and put them on her younger son Jacob. She also covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the goatskins. Then she handed to her son Jacob the tasty food and the bread she had made." - Gen 27:14-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Watch how much effort goes into this deception. Rebekah cooks the meal to taste just like Esau's. She dresses Jacob in Esau's best clothes so he will smell like his brother. She even covers his hands and neck with goatskins to fake Esau's hairiness. No detail is left out. Sin, it turns out, can be remarkably careful and creative.

There is a sober lesson here. We sometimes imagine that wrongdoing is careless or lazy, but often it is the opposite — thoughtful, planned, and thorough. People will pour real energy into covering their tracks, arranging the perfect lie, making a deception seamless. The same cleverness God gives us for good can be bent toward deceit.

It is worth asking honestly: where am I putting careful effort into something I know is wrong? A well-planned deception is still a deception, however skillfully done. All the goatskins in the world cannot make a lie honest.

Imagine if this family had poured the same energy into trusting God and doing what was right. God calls us to use our gifts, our planning, and our creativity in the light — for truth, for good, for His glory (Col 3:9-10). Let our best efforts serve honesty, not cover for sin.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I putting careful effort into something I know is wrong?
2. Am I using my gifts and creativity for truth or for cover-up?
3. What would it look like to redirect that energy toward doing right?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for any effort I put into hiding what is wrong. Help me to use my gifts and creativity in the light, for truth and for Your glory. Amen.
